summary: Describes YANG mechanisms for defining abstract data structures, meaning structures that are not part of a configuration datastore. For example, they can describe message contents.

plainLanguage.summary: A blueprint for a shape of data that is not tied to a particular device settings list.

questions: how to define abstract data structures in yang
what is the yang structure extension
subtitle: Two YANG extensions for defining abstract data structures that are not configuration or operational state.

tldr.problem: Protocol messages and files need to be described in YANG without being configuration or state, and the older yang-data extension was limited and hard to extend.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a structure extension to declare an abstract data structure, and an augment-structure extension to add nodes to one from another module.
tldr.outcome: Specifications can model whole or nested messages and let external documents extend them, using the same tree-diagram and encoding conventions as other YANG data.

today: RFC 8791 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated. It updates RFC 8340 with the tree-diagram sections for structures.

sections.title: Why Abstract Data Structures
sections.content:
There is a need for standard ways to define abstract data that is not meant to be implemented as configuration or operational state. The yang-data extension from RFC 8040 was defined for this purpose, but its functionality is limited. It was meant to model all or part of a protocol message, such as the errors definition in ietf-restconf, or the contents of a file.

Protocols are often layered so that the header or payload of a message can be extended by external documents, and the YANG that models them needs to support that. This RFC therefore defines structure, which is more flexible than yang-data and can be nested inside another data structure, and augment-structure, which is similar to the YANG augment statement.

The ordinary augment statement cannot be used on these structures because a YANG compiler or other tool is not required to understand the structure extension.
sections.plainLanguage: Some information is not settings for a machine, like a letter that gets sent between machines. YANG needed a better way to describe the shape of such letters and let others add to them.

sections.title: Defining a YANG Data Structure
sections.content:
A YANG data structure is defined with the structure extension statement from the module ietf-yang-structure-ext. Its argument is the name of the structure. Structure names share the identifier namespace of RFC 7950, so a structure cannot have the same name as a sibling node or another structure in the same module.

A structure does not have to be used as a top-level message. The extension itself is valid only as a top-level statement in a module or submodule, but the structure it defines may be used elsewhere. The extension does not define a media type, so a specification using it MUST specify the message encoding rules, including the content media type where applicable.

A structure is encoded like an anydata node: the structure name becomes a container, and the instantiated children are encoded as its child nodes. The module name and namespace are assigned to each data definition inside it. Two constraints apply inside a structure: a list is not required to have a key, and a config statement is ignored.
sections.plainLanguage: You give the shape a name, and then fill it with the boxes it should have. Two names cannot be the same in one place, and boxes do not need to be marked as settings.

sections.title: Augmenting a Structure
sections.content:
The augment-structure extension adds data to a structure defined with structure. Its argument is a path, an absolute-schema-nodeid whose first node identifies the structure and whose remaining nodes identify the node to augment. It is also valid only as a top-level statement.

Its substatements follow the rules of the augment statement: optional status, description and reference, then one or more data definitions or cases. The context node is derived as for augment in RFC 7950, and the same list and config constraints apply.

For example, module foo defines foo-data with a container foo-con, and module bar uses augment-structure /foo:foo-data/foo:foo-con to add two leafs, add-leaf1 and add-leaf2.
sections.plainLanguage: Someone else can tape a new box onto your form without changing your original. That is what augmenting does.

sections.title: Tree Diagrams
sections.content:
This RFC updates RFC 8340, which defines YANG tree diagrams, by adding two new sections to a module's diagram. Structures are shown after the keyword structure with the structure name and a colon, and augmentations after augment-structure with the target structure name and a colon. Both are offset by two spaces.

Nodes inside structures are printed by the rules in Section 2.6 of RFC 8340, except that they do not have any flags.
sections.plainLanguage: When people draw a picture of the shape, the new kinds of boxes get their own labelled sections so that readers can tell them apart.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The appendix defines an address-book structure holding a list of address entries keyed by last first, with leafs for last name, first name, street, city and state. A second module uses augment-structure to add county and zipcode leafs. The data is shown encoded in both XML and JSON, with the added zipcode carrying its own module namespace.

Another example defines my-example-error-info with an error-code leaf and shows it nested in the <error-info> element of an <rpc-error>. This shows a structure used as a non-top-level element.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples show an address book that someone else adds a postal code to, and an error note tucked inside a bigger message.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The RFC says it defines YANG extensions used for conceptual data structures and does not introduce any new vulnerabilities beyond those in YANG 1.1 (RFC 7950).

IANA registered the XML namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-yang-structure-ext and the YANG module ietf-yang-structure-ext with prefix sx.
sections.plainLanguage: This only describes shapes of information, so it adds no new dangers by itself.

viz.caption: TREE DIAGRAM FROM RFC 8791 APPENDIX A.1

data.title: address-book structure
data.code:
module: example-module

  structure address-book:
    +-- address* [last first]
       +-- last      string
       +-- first     string
       +-- street?   string
       +-- city?     string
       +-- state?    string
